note: Week 2026-08-24 build. Prior 8/17-8/21 book closed at official Fri 8/21 SIP closes for -5606.67 realized - the worst week since inception, with 14 of 15 names red. The book was ~70% technology into a week when info tech shed more than 3% and a bond-market selloff (Treasury's doubled long-end buyback did not steady the tape) hit high-multiple growth; FN -23.4% on its 8/17 print, CRWV -16.5%, RDDT -13.9%, KEYS -11.7% and WMT -10.0% on its sales miss did the damage, with only DE (+6.3%) green. This week deliberately rotates out of that concentration and into what is actually working, confirmed by fresh catalysts: (1) metals - copper at record Comex highs on a supply squeeze (FCX closed Friday at a 52-week high after PT hikes) and gold near three-month highs with GDX +23.75% in August, its best month since April 2020; (2) energy - Brent near $89 with the Strait of Hormuz still closed after US-Iran talks collapsed, COP at a 52-week high; (3) crypto-levered financials - bitcoin's best week since March 2023 (+22% to $77,000+) on the SEC's 8/18 'Regulation Crypto Assets' proposal and the White House push for the CLARITY Act, with HOOD +13.6% Friday and COIN +8%; (4) fresh single-stock catalysts - MRK at a 52-week high on the first-ever positive Phase 3 for an individualized neoantigen cancer therapy, TGT at a 52-week high on a beat-and-raise, F on a Jefferies upgrade to Buy. Tech exposure is cut to two names, both held for in-window prints: NVDA Wed 8/26 AMC (guided $91.0B +/- 2%, street $91.9-95B) and MRVL Thu 8/27 AMC. DY (Wed) and ULTA (Thu) round out the in-window earnings sleeve at small size. Macro risk sits at the end of the window: Jackson Hole runs 8/27-8/29 and Chair Warsh delivers his first keynote as Chair on Friday 8/28 - a hawkish lean would compress September cut odds, lift real yields and pressure both the gold sleeve and the high-multiple names. 14 names, ~89.9% deployed, ~10.1% cash. Entries recorded at verified Fri 8/21 SIP closes; positions open Monday 8/24.

positions.name: Freeport-McMoRan
positions.catalyst: Copper broke to record Comex highs through August on a deepening global supply squeeze, falling Chinese refined output and pending US copper tariff decisions; FCX closed Friday at a fresh 52-week high (+7.6% on the session) after Q2 adj EPS of $0.74 vs $0.59 consensus and a wave of PT hikes (Wells Fargo to Overweight/$70, Barclays $82, Argus $78).
positions.risks: No company-specific catalyst in-window; a copper tariff resolution or Chinese demand wobble unwinds the squeeze fast; closed exactly at its 52-week high, so no cushion.
positions.driver: Strongest confirmed momentum in the materials complex on a live commodity catalyst.

positions.name: Merck & Co.
positions.catalyst: Merck and Moderna's Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial of intismeran autogene + KEYTRUDA hit both recurrence-free and distant-metastasis-free survival endpoints in resected stage IIB-IV melanoma on 8/19 - the first positive Phase 3 for an individualized neoantigen therapy and the first to beat KEYTRUDA monotherapy. MRK jumped 7% and closed Friday at a 52-week high of $152.55.
positions.risks: Closed at its 52-week high with no in-window follow-on catalyst; the readout is topline only, with full data at a later medical meeting; large-cap pharma beta is low so upside is capped.
positions.driver: Fresh, franchise-extending clinical catalyst that de-risks the KEYTRUDA patent cliff.

positions.name: Target
positions.catalyst: Q2 on 8/19 beat across the board - net sales $26.5B (+5.3%), comps +3.8% vs 2.4% consensus, EPS $4.11 vs $2.05 a year ago - and management raised FY26 EPS guidance to $9.90-$10.90 from $7.50-$8.50 with sales to ~$110.0B. Stock printed a fresh 52-week high and held it into Friday's close.
positions.risks: Catalyst is behind it, so this is post-beat drift; July retail sales fell 0.6% MoM; a two-quarter turnaround is not yet a trend.
positions.driver: Post-earnings momentum with a raised guide - the one retailer whose bar went up, not down.

positions.name: Newmont
positions.catalyst: Gold pushed to a near three-month high on 8/21 on a softer dollar and falling long-end yields after Treasury doubled its 20- and 30-year buybacks; the VanEck Gold Miners ETF gained 23.75% in August, its best month since April 2020. Newmont's Q2 realized price of $4,414/oz drove a record $2.2B of quarterly free cash flow.
positions.risks: No in-window company catalyst; a hawkish Warsh at Jackson Hole on Friday 8/28 would lift real yields and hit bullion; the August move is already large.
positions.driver: Highest-FCF leverage to a gold tape making new highs on a live macro catalyst.

positions.name: ConocoPhillips
positions.catalyst: Brent is holding near $89 with the Strait of Hormuz - roughly a fifth of seaborne crude - still closed after US-Iran talks to reopen it collapsed. COP closed Friday at a 52-week high of $134.87, the cleanest large-cap E&P leverage to the price of the barrel.
positions.risks: A surprise diplomatic breakthrough on Hormuz could send Brent toward $70 and unwind the entire trade in a session; no company catalyst in-window.
positions.driver: Pure-play E&P momentum at a 52-week high confirmed by an unresolved supply shock.

positions.name: Exxon Mobil
positions.catalyst: Same Hormuz supply shock, but with integrated downstream and chemicals to absorb it: XOM is up roughly 29-31% YTD as XLE gained over 21%, and refining margins are widening as rerouted barrels lengthen voyages. Trades ~6% below its March 52-week high of $176.41, so it is not extended.
positions.risks: No in-window catalyst; a Hormuz reopening compresses both crude and crack spreads; mega-cap energy lags the E&Ps on any spike.
positions.driver: Lower-beta way to hold the energy momentum with room to the prior high.

positions.name: Agnico Eagle Mines
positions.catalyst: Second leg of the gold trade and the highest-quality operator in it - $1.3B of Q2 free cash flow at $1,459 AISC, the widest margin in the senior producer group, into bullion at record levels. Sits ~15% below its March 52-week high of $255.24, so the August miner rally has not yet re-rated it fully.
positions.risks: No company catalyst in-window; correlated one-for-one with NEM, so the gold sleeve moves together; Jackson Hole is the obvious reversal risk.
positions.driver: Best-margin senior gold producer with catch-up room versus the sector's August move.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.catalyst: Q2 FY27 results Wed 8/26 AMC - the single largest scheduled event of the week. Company guided to $91.0B +/- 2%; the sell side is modeling $91.9B-$95B (roughly 67-75% YoY) on a Blackwell ramp with data center alone potentially above $80B, and EPS consensus of $2.07-$2.08. Analyst targets cluster $275-$325.
positions.risks: Binary print mid-week that sets the tone for the whole tape; NVDA fell 4.6% last week as info tech shed more than 3%; China policy commentary is an unquantifiable swing factor.
positions.driver: The marquee in-window catalyst, entered after a 9% drawdown from the May high.

positions.name: Coinbase Global
positions.catalyst: Bitcoin's best week since March 2023 - up ~22% to above $77,000 - on genuine policy catalysts: the SEC proposed 'Regulation Crypto Assets' on 8/18 (its first crypto rulemaking rather than an enforcement action, with a $75M token safe harbor) and Trump publicly pushed Congress on the CLARITY Act. COIN gained ~8% on Friday; Q2 showed 10.3% trading share and a 14th straight positive adjusted-EBITDA quarter.
positions.risks: Highest-beta name in the book - a bitcoin reversal cuts it twice as hard; still ~54% below its October 52-week high; rulemaking is a proposal, not a rule.
positions.driver: Direct equity expression of a crypto tape making its biggest weekly move in two years.

positions.name: Robinhood Markets
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday around $108, +13.6% on the session and +13% on the week, its best week since July 2, on the same crypto-regulation catalyst plus Vlad Tenev's widely-circulated 8/18 push for domestic tokenized equities and continued private-market product expansion.
positions.risks: Friday's move was enormous and invites profit-taking; 47x earnings; retail engagement falls off fast if the crypto bid fades.
positions.driver: Fastest-moving name in the financials complex on the week's clearest policy catalyst.

positions.name: Ford Motor
positions.catalyst: Jefferies upgraded Ford to Buy with a $17.50 target on 8/21, arguing Q2 marked the volume trough as production and US demand recover; shares rose more than 6% after Q2 earnings topped expectations and full-year core profit guidance moved higher. Trades at $14.41 against a $17.78 52-week high.
positions.risks: Deep-cyclical exposure into a tape worried about oil-driven inflation; tariff and warranty costs remain live; the stock has repeatedly failed to hold rallies over the past year.
positions.driver: Fresh sell-side upgrade on top of a beat-and-raise, with a clear gap to the prior high.

positions.name: Marvell Technology
positions.catalyst: Q2 FY27 results Thu 8/27 AMC, consensus $0.87 EPS. Management has guided optical interconnect revenue to grow above 70% YoY in FY27 - outpacing custom AI silicon at 20%+ - with a design-win pipeline above 50 opportunities and the $12B Google custom-chip relationship validating the ASIC platform. 25 of 35 covering analysts rate it Strong Buy.
positions.risks: Sold off ~6% on Friday alone (open $252.39, close $237.04), so short-term momentum is negative going in; 53x forward earnings and 16.5x sales leave no room for a soft custom-silicon ramp; binary print.
positions.driver: In-window earnings catalyst in the second-best AI interconnect franchise, entered on a pullback.

positions.name: Dycom Industries
positions.catalyst: FQ2 FY27 results Wed 8/26 - the company carries a record $11.9B backlog (+25% sequentially, 2.2x book-to-bill) with $6.4B due in the next twelve months, FQ1 revenue +56.1% YoY to $1.96B, and the Power Solutions acquisition has pivoted it into AI data centers where over 90% of that segment serves hyperscalers. FY27 revenue guidance was raised to $7.38-$7.65B.
positions.risks: Trades ~31% below its May 52-week high of $566.47, so momentum is against it going into the print; thin float and low liquidity make the earnings reaction violent in both directions; smallest position in the book for that reason.
positions.driver: Highest-visibility AI-infrastructure backlog in the book with an in-window print.

positions.name: Ulta Beauty
positions.catalyst: Q2 results Thu 8/27 AMC, consensus $6.21 EPS (+7.4% YoY) on $2.98B revenue (+6.9%), with AI-guided shopping being pushed to lift conversion. The stock has stabilized in the low $500s after basing at $443.60 on 6/30, so the bar into the print is materially lower than it was in February.
positions.risks: Still ~27% below its February 52-week high, so this is a mean-reversion earnings bet rather than a momentum trade; discretionary beauty spend is exposed to the same consumer softness that hit WMT last week.
positions.driver: In-window earnings catalyst where sentiment has already been reset.
